Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Civic life: news, government & the law

rule noun

a regulation

also rules, regulation, the rules, house rules, break the rules, follow the rules, guideline, guidelines, rule of thumb, lay down rules, observe the rule

classical

Cic. Amic. 44: haec igitur prīma lēx amīcitiae sanciātur
Cic. Amic. 40 (Lewis & Short)

lēx, lēgis f.

noun, third declension

a rule, a regulation; a condition

Besides the laws of the state, any rule laid down for how a thing is done (Lewis & Short: “a law, precept, regulation, principle, rule”). eā lēge ut, on condition that (Plaut. Most. 2.1.13, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • rēgula, rēgulae f. — a rule, a standard

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.110: nostrae nātūrae rēgulā mētiāmur; Traupman 248, 372–373

    Properly a ruler (see ruler), then a standard to measure by. Traupman uses it for rules in general: rēgulam servāre, to keep the rule; rēgulam frangere, to break it (pp. 372–373).

  • praeceptum, praeceptī n. — a precept, an instruction

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 2.51: hoc praeceptum officiī dīligenter tenendum est; Sen. Ep. 6.5: longum iter est per praecepta

    A rule given as advice or instruction, by a teacher or a parent.

Examples

  • haec igitur prīma lēx amīcitiae sanciātur, ut ab amīcīs honesta petāmus, amīcōrum causā honesta faciāmus

    let this, then, be the first rule of friendship: to ask friends only for what is right, and to do only what is right for their sakeCic. Amic. 44

  • rēgulam frangere

    to break the ruleTraupman 373

  • rēgulam servāre

    to follow (observe) the ruleTraupman 373

  • rēgulās īnstituere

    to lay down rulesTraupman 373

See also law, follow, ruler, rule.
